cat >> README.md <<'EOF'

## Error tracking
Errors are reported to Sentry when `SENTRY_DSN` is set (optional: `SENTRY_RELEASE`, `SENTRY_TRACES_SAMPLE_RATE`, `NODE_ENV`). Without a DSN it is a no-op. Always start via `npm start` so `src/instrument.js` loads first.
EOF

text:
I added Sentry error tracking. The server starts cleanly with the new setup, but I haven't sent a real error to Sentry. That needs a DSN, which I don't have.

- **Dependency:** I installed `@sentry/node`.
- **`src/instrument.js` (new):** This initializes Sentry. It does nothing unless `SENTRY_DSN` is set, so no data leaves the app by default. Optional settings are `SENTRY_RELEASE`, `SENTRY_TRACES_SAMPLE_RATE` (default 0) and `NODE_ENV`.
- **`src/server.js`:** I added `Sentry.setupExpressErrorHandler(app)` after the routes. A failed `pg` query in the async `/households/:id/lists` handler is now captured. Express 5 passes those failures to the error handler. I also added a fallback handler that returns a JSON 500 instead of Express's default HTML error page.
- **`package.json`:** `npm start` now runs `node --import ./src/instrument.js src/server.js`. Sentry has to load before `express` and `pg` so it can instrument them. If you start the app another way, errors won't be tracked.
- **`README.md`:** I added a short note on the setup.

To turn it on, create a Sentry project and set `SENTRY_DSN` in your deploy environment.
